findings.location: amendment.json changes[HI-7, REFINED].shares["HE-008"] (and the README row generated from it)
findings.finding: The HE-008 OBSERVER share drops one carried item: no process setrlimit/getrlimit for planeon_observer_t on other domains. HE-004A's R10 record carries it to HE-008 (MODEL_DEFINED.md at a34a429, HE-004A 'Carried': "no setrlimit/getrlimit on other domains (prlimit64 is unconditional in the OBSERVER row)"). DESIGN-A section 1 carries it too. Design review A round 1, D1-6 item (3), asked the next W03-plan meta packet to record it as an HE-008 OBSERVER share (G5). Every other carried HE-008 item is in the share. Amendment 1's EFFECT_GATE share has the same clause ("with no process setrlimit on other domains"). This item makes up for a seccomp rule that is unconditional, so leaving it out drops a security constraint from the register.
findings.requiredChange: Add to the HI-7 HE-008 share: "no process setrlimit or getrlimit for planeon_observer_t on other domains (prlimit64 is unconditional in the OBSERVER row)". Then regenerate the README.

findings.finding: Owner decision Q-HE4A-B2 (a) (OWNER_DECISIONS.md:53) states: "SEC-4 for OBSERVER rests on: the digest- and length-pinned programs, present exactly once per binary; the post-seal and linked-source rules; and T04's installed-filter proof." The contract does not quote Q-HE4A-B2 (DRAFT.md section 1 planned to), and SEC-4's packet list after the change has no T04. The same decision dropped the wrapper inventory, so T04's proof that the installed filter equals the OBSERVER digest is one of SEC-4's three stated legs for OBSERVER, and no plan packet owns it. HE-004A's carried T04 items have no packet either (MODEL_DEFINED 'Carried'/T04; DESIGN-A section 1): the installed filter equals the OBSERVER digest, Seccomp_filters: 1, the post-seal exit-path trace, PR_CAPBSET_READ(41) returns EINVAL, and TSYNC and dumpability at exec.
findings.requiredChange: Quote Q-HE4A-B2 verbatim: its SEC-4 bullet and its inventory bullets, with the classifier-stop context as recorded. Add a SEC-4 PACKETS_ADDED row (+T04) with the share "for OBSERVER: the installed filter equals the OBSERVER digest (Seccomp_filters: 1)". For the other carried T04 checks (CAP_LAST_CAP, TSYNC and dumpability at exec, the exit-path trace), add T04 to HI-7, or state where they live. This is not a T04 design.

findings.finding: Q-HE4-2 is called an owner decision in two places: I06-2's source ("owner decisions Q-HE4-2 (a)") and the README ("split by owner decision Q-HE4-2 (a)"). OWNER_DECISIONS.md:11-12 lists Q-HE4-2 under 'Monitor (owner-delegated)'. The contract's own ownerDecisions entry and the NP-3, SEC-4 and HI-7 sources call it a monitor decision.
findings.requiredChange: I06-2 source: "monitor decisions Q-HE4-2 (a), Q-HE4B-1 (a), Q-HE4B-10 (a)+(c), Q-HE4B-11 (b)". README: "split by the monitor's owner-delegated decision Q-HE4-2 (a)".

findings.finding: The text says "No wrapper classifier, table or inventory is built, by any route." The owner's scope sentence is "No agent builds a wrapper classifier, table or inventory, by any route, now or at T04." The contract drops the rule's subject (agents) and its time scope. The obligation therefore forbids more than the owner did: it also forbids a human-curated list, which Q-HE4A-B2 named as a possible route.
findings.requiredChange: Use the owner's sentence: "No agent builds a wrapper classifier, table or inventory, by any route, now or at T04."

findings.finding: (a) The parenthetical "(cgroup.procs, pidfd_open, the stat start time, cgroup.procs again, the pidfd still alive)" comes right after "every v3 check", so it reads as the list of v3 checks. It lists the five observation steps (I05 v4 README:64-70). The v3 checks are peer, state, outstanding actions, replay, generation, binding, certificate and manifest reuse (README:56-57). (b) README:332-333 says "The observation on a real kernel (pidfd and stat behaviour, the bounds in rule 5) is native work for R10's adoption and T04", but I05-7 names only HE-003A3.
findings.requiredChange: Move the parenthetical after "observes the BIND's worker", or name the v3 checks. Add T04, citing README:332-333, with the share "the observation on a real kernel: pidfd and stat behaviour and rule 5's bounds".

findings.finding: (a) "The gate obtains its cgroup2-root and /proc directory fds at start" is gate code (README:179: "R10 obtains the two root directory fds at start, under C2"), but HE-003A3 is not in I05-8's packets or shares, so no packet owns that clause. (b) The source's cgroup2-root precondition is the gate's dir search there (status.json:190 "the cgroup2 root's dir search (IR1-7)"; README:179-180 and :345). The text instead says "the cgroup2 root's own type is host policy", which is a fact, not an obligation, and HE-008's share repeats the vague "the cgroup2 root's host policy". (c) "one time namespace" drops the source's "or at least one boottime offset" (README:157 and :342).
findings.requiredChange: Give the root-fd clause to HE-003A3, either as an I05-8 packet with that share or by moving the clause to I05-7. State the precondition as "host policy grants the gate dir search on the cgroup2 root (T04 checks it)". Keep "one time namespace, or at least one boottime offset".

findings.finding: The cited line (corrected HOST_INTERFACE_SPEC.md:52) defines I01 as "AF_UNIX/SOCK_SEQPACKET /run/planeon/live-proxy/policy-observer.sock; only OBSERVE_POLICY; exact current request/response schema". It sits under 'Existing interfaces — byte-compatible, no changes now'. The ADDED text keeps AF_UNIX and OBSERVE_POLICY but drops SOCK_SEQPACKET, the socket path, 'only' and the exact current schema. As written, the obligation does not bind HE-004-I01 to the existing byte-compatible contract.
findings.requiredChange: Add the spec line's terms. For example: "... produces I01 as the existing contract defines it: AF_UNIX SOCK_SEQPACKET on /run/planeon/live-proxy/policy-observer.sock, only OBSERVE_POLICY, the exact current request/response schema (byte-compatible), after ...".

findings.finding: (a) The ADDED definition names text, source, packets and scope, but OBS-INV-1 and I05-8 also carry shares. The REFINED definition covers only replacing the packet, but every REFINED row carries shares. The SEC-4 and HI-7 REFINED rows also give a share to HE-008, which is not one of the parts; only shareRule's new last sentence allows that. (b) No rule says how a share combines with an earlier share of the same packet: HE-008 already holds amendment 1's EFFECT_GATE shares in SEC-4 and HI-7. (c) refinementRule does not require every obligation that lists HE-004 after amendment 1 to have a REFINED row. That holds today (6 of 6: ADM-4, HI-7, I06-2, I06-3, NP-3, SEC-4), but the checker proves the rule, not today's content.
findings.requiredChange: Make each one-line definition name the shares its rows may carry (REFINED: shares for its parts and, under shareRule, for other packets in the list). Add a sentence that a share adds to the packet's earlier shares. Add to refinementRule: "every obligation whose post-amendment-1 list names the refined packet has exactly one REFINED row".

findings.finding: The HE-008 share includes "the observer's RBAC grants, which follow HE-004B1's request specs (decided with HE-004C)". HI-7 is "Per-role uid, capabilities, seccomp and SELinux", and Kubernetes RBAC grants fall outside that text. The I06 v1 closure also gives User planeon:policy-observer allowedGrants [] (identity-closure.json:1765-1774 at fd362f9e). Grants that only HE-008 provisions would therefore fail the observer's own IC check. The HE-004 dossier's Q-HE4-6 recommendation and the carried G5-G7 ("RBAC provisioning, W02-PROD") give the naming to the I06 successor. Q-HE4-6 is still to be decided with C.
findings.requiredChange: Move the RBAC grants out of HI-7. Either add their own obligation naming HE-004C (decides, Q-HE4-6), HE-008 (provisions) and W02G-F2 (the closure names them), or state the closure dependency and leave the row to the packet that decides Q-HE4-6.
